What is Simple Interest?

Simple Interest (SI) is a quick and straightforward method of calculating the interest charge on a loan or earned on a deposit. The interest is calculated only on the original principal amount and doesn't compound over time.

Unlike compound interest where interest earns interest, simple interest provides linear growth. This makes it ideal for short-term loans, certain bonds, and basic financial calculations.

हिंदी में: साधारण ब्याज (Simple Interest) सिर्फ मूल राशि पर लगाया जाता है। समय बढ़ने पर भी ब्याज की राशि हर साल समान रहती है। यह छोटी अवधि के लोन और बेसिक हिसाब के लिए सबसे अच्छा है।

Simple Interest Formula

SI = (P × R × T) / 100

  • • SI = Simple Interest
  • • P = Principal Amount
  • • R = Rate of Interest per annum (%)
  • • T = Time period in years

Total Amount = Principal + Simple Interest

A = P + SI = P(1 + RT/100)

Where is SI Used?

Car Loans

Most auto loans use simple interest method

Personal Loans (Short-term)

Quick personal loans often use SI

Treasury Bills

Government short-term securities

Certificate of Deposits

Inter-personal Lending

Money lent between individuals

Educational Examples

Most school-level math problems

Solved Example

Problem: Calculate simple interest on ₹50,000 at 10% per annum for 5 years.

Given: P = ₹50,000, R = 10%, T = 5 years

SI = (P × R × T) / 100

SI = (50,000 × 10 × 5) / 100

SI = 25,00,000 / 100

SI = ₹25,000

Total Amount = 50,000 + 25,000 = ₹75,000

Frequently Asked Questions

Everything about Simple Interest calculations

What is simple interest?▼
Simple Interest (SI) is interest calculated only on the original principal amount throughout the loan or deposit period. Unlike compound interest, it doesn't earn interest on previously earned interest, providing linear growth.
What is the formula for simple interest?▼
The simple interest formula is: SI = (P × R × T) / 100, where P is Principal, R is annual Rate of interest, and T is Time in years. To find total amount, use: A = P + SI = P(1 + RT/100).
How do you calculate simple interest with example?▼
Example: For ₹10,000 at 10% interest for 5 years: SI = (10000 × 10 × 5) / 100 = ₹5,000. So total amount payable/receivable = ₹10,000 + ₹5,000 = ₹15,000.
How to calculate simple interest for months?▼
For monthly calculation: SI = (P × R × T) / (100 × 12), where T is months. Example: ₹10,000 at 12% for 6 months = (10000 × 12 × 6) / (100 × 12) = ₹600.
How to calculate simple interest for days?▼
For daily calculation: SI = (P × R × T) / (100 × 365), where T is number of days. Example: ₹10,000 at 10% for 90 days = (10000 × 10 × 90) / (100 × 365) = ₹246.58.
What is the difference between simple and compound interest?▼
Simple interest is calculated only on the principal amount. Compound interest is calculated on principal plus accumulated interest. CI grows exponentially faster than SI - so CI is better for investments but worse for loans.
Which is better - simple or compound interest?▼
For BORROWERS: Simple interest is better (you pay less). For INVESTORS: Compound interest is better (you earn more). Example: ₹1 lakh at 10% for 10 years = SI ₹1 lakh vs CI ₹1.59 lakh interest.
Where is simple interest used in India?▼
Simple interest is commonly used for: (1) Car loans and auto financing, (2) Short-term personal loans, (3) Treasury Bills (T-Bills), (4) Some types of bonds, (5) Money lent between individuals, (6) Educational math problems.
Do banks use simple or compound interest?▼
Banks mostly use compound interest for: Savings accounts, Fixed Deposits (FDs), Recurring Deposits (RDs), Home loans, EMI loans. They use simple interest for: Some auto loans, certain short-term loans, T-bills.
How to find principal from simple interest?▼
To find Principal: P = (SI × 100) / (R × T). Example: If SI is ₹2,000 at 8% for 5 years, then P = (2000 × 100) / (8 × 5) = ₹5,000.
How to find rate of interest in simple interest?▼
To find Rate: R = (SI × 100) / (P × T). Example: For SI ₹500 on ₹10,000 for 1 year, R = (500 × 100) / (10000 × 1) = 5% per annum.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is simple interest formula?

Simple Interest = (Principal × Rate × Time) / 100. Total amount = Principal + Simple Interest. It is linear and calculated only on original principal.

When is simple interest used in India?

Simple interest is used in short-term personal loans, vehicle loans initial calculations, some government schemes, and educational understanding of interest concepts.

What is difference between simple and compound interest?

Simple interest is calculated on principal only and grows linearly. Compound interest grows on principal plus accumulated interest and increases exponentially.

Is simple interest better for borrowers?

Yes. Borrowers pay less with simple interest compared to compound interest for same rate and tenure. Compound interest costs more over long periods.

Does any Indian bank offer simple interest on savings?

Most Indian banks offer simple interest on savings accounts calculated daily or quarterly. FDs typically use compound interest for better growth.

How to calculate EMI using simple interest?

Basic EMI = (Principal + Simple Interest) / Number of months. For accurate EMI, use compound reducing balance method which most banks use for home and car loans.
